title: Saudi oil shows why the next OPEC+ production increase could deliver less than markets expect
summary: Saudi Arabia can send oil from its eastern fields to an overseas customer without putting a tanker through the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow passage connecting the Persian Gulf to the open sea. The crude travels by pipeline across the country to Yanbu, a port on the Red Sea, where a ship collects it.
